chapter_title: The Breaking of the Sacrificial Bow
verification_note: Chapter text and translations for verses 1–12 checked online. Narration paraphrases are not quotations.

entries.fact: Kṛṣṇa meets Trivakrā with fragrant ointments on the royal road.
Kṛṣṇa asks about the ointments and requests some for Himself and Balarāma.
She serves Kaṁsa making ointments and offers them to the brothers.
Trivakrā generously gives ointment to Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.
The brothers are adorned with ointment and appear beautiful.
Kṛṣṇa is pleased and decides to straighten Trivakrā.
Kṛṣṇa presses her toes with His feet and lifts her chin, straightening her body.
entries.adaptation: Gentle composition is an artistic choice.

entries.fact: Trivakrā is transformed with straight, proportionate limbs.
entries.adaptation: Non-sensational depiction; worth is not tied to appearance.

entries.fact: Trivakrā takes hold of Kṛṣṇa's upper cloth and addresses Him.
entries.adaptation: Gesture omitted; longing summarized for children.

entries.fact: Trivakrā invites Kṛṣṇa to her home.
Kṛṣṇa glances at Balarāma and the cowherd boys before replying.
Kṛṣṇa says He will visit after fulfilling His purpose.
